text: Then the lake turned on them.
The Sea of Galilee lies seven hundred feet below sea level, in a bowl of hills — when cold wind spills down those slopes, calm water can turn violent in minutes.
This storm was savage even by that lake's standard.
Waves broke over the side faster than the men could bail.
And the fishermen who had survived a hundred storms looked at this one — and believed it was going to be their last.
